sessions.title: Test day 1
sessions.note: Cirque was 11 days ago and you are recovered. Test first, train after.

why.purpose: Every load in this program is a percentage of a tested number. A guessed max produces guessed training, and 54 weeks of it compounds into a plan that fits somebody else.
why.know: Test rested and log honestly. Sandbagging costs a block of correct loading. Overreaching costs a week of recovery and a number you cannot repeat.

items.name: Front squat 3RM

items.name: Bench 3RM

items.name: Log everything in src/athlete.ts

items.name: Strict press 3RM
items.prescription: standing, no leg drive, from the rack
items.cue: The gate on the strict HSPU. At 237 bodyweight you need roughly 178-190 to be in range.

items.name: Deadlift 3RM
items.prescription: you did 500x3 cold, so open conservatively

items.name: Deadlift heavy single
items.cue: Your tested 525 underperforms your rep max. Practice expressing a max.

why.purpose: Front squat is the gate on a 315 clean and jerk and it needs 28 weeks of runway, not 15. Bench frequency starts here because upper-body pressing costs almost nothing against fat loss or running.

items.name: Front squat
items.cue: Elbows up. The gate on a 315 clean and jerk.

items.name: Strict pull-up
items.cue: Sets across at bodyweight. Your max is 5, so triples are the right dose. Do not grind.

why.purpose: Your jerk sits below your clean, which is backwards for almost everyone. That is a technique and overhead-confidence problem, and the fix is repeated exposure to good positions, not heavier loads.
why.know: Quality reps beat heavy reps. If a rep looked ugly it did not count. Stop at the prescribed sets even if you feel good, because the adaptation you want is a motor pattern and fatigue corrupts it.

items.name: Strict press
items.cue: Linear, not percentage-based. Add 5 lb when the prescription says to and the reps are clean.

items.name: Seated DB press
items.cue: No leg drive. Deep range.

items.cue: Footwork over load. Your jerk sits below your clean and that is technical.

why.purpose: Complexes force you to hold positions across movements in a row, exposing technical leaks that single reps hide. Moderate load is deliberate: teaching, not testing.
why.know: Stop when technique degrades, not when the clock says to. Every ugly rep is practice at doing it wrong.

items.name: Snatch complex
items.prescription: 5 x 1 power snatch + 1 hang snatch + 1 OHS @ 84%

why.purpose: Optional easy spin to move blood without adding stress.
why.know: Winter in Bozeman, a new job, an infant. The honest answer most weeks is take the day off.

sessions.title: Snatch + jumps
sessions.note: Dunk attempt window is open. Chalk up and find a hoop this week.

why.stimulus: Rate of force development · motor pattern
why.purpose: Your snatch is 67% of your clean when normal is 78-82%. That is the cheapest gain on the whole list and it is technical, not strength. Jumps share the day because both are maximal-velocity qualities and belong together while you are fresh.
why.know: Speed work first, always, and never to fatigue. The moment bar speed or jump height drops you are training a different quality than the one you came for.

items.name: Intensive plyos
items.cue: 60-80 contacts. Fully fresh. Stop the moment quality drops.

why.purpose: Front squat drives toward 340. The clean you can catch is capped by the squat you can stand up out of.
why.know: This lift decides whether C&J 315 is a this-year goal. If it climbs faster than projected, revisit the target mid-block.

items.name: Ring muscle-up
items.cue: Needs the high anchor. If it is not built, substitute low-ring transitions.

items.name: Front squat
items.cue: Driving toward 340. This is the gate on the clean and jerk.

sessions.title: Zone 2
sessions.note: Bike. Non-negotiable.

why.purpose: Two sessions weekly is roughly the floor for holding aerobic adaptation. Preservation is far cheaper than rebuilding.
why.know: Tempting to cut in a power block. Do not. Losing the base over winter is what puts the Crest out of reach in August.

sessions.title: Clean & jerk
sessions.note: Dunk attempt window is open. Chalk up and find a hoop this week.

why.stimulus: Rate of force development · overhead · maximal velocity
why.purpose: The C&J is limited by your jerk, so percentages run off the jerk max. Jerk recoveries load above that max in the rack to build the overhead confidence the lift lacks.
why.know: Technical-phase percentages are capped on purpose. Weightlifting is a skill sport and long sets degrade the pattern you are encoding.

items.name: Clean & jerk
items.cue: Percentage is off your jerk, not your clean. The jerk is the limiter.

why.purpose: Sprints sit at the far velocity end of the force-velocity curve, past what a barbell can train. They feed the dunk and cost little recovery when kept short.
why.know: Sprints go before the squat, full recovery between reps, 20-30 m not 60. The treadmill cannot do this.

items.name: Sprint accelerations
items.cue: Treadmill will not do this. Pavement or a field.

sessions.note: This is the window. Light plyo warm-up, then a hoop and 20 honest attempts.

blocks.name: Strip & Skill
blocks.goal: Cut 28 lbs, bank gymnastics skill, build front squat and jerk early.
principles: A caloric deficit is a poor environment for building. This block preserves and learns skills instead.
Intensity preserves lean mass, volume fatigues. 3-5 sets of 3-5 at 80-88%, no circuits.
Relative strength goals get cheaper as bodyweight drops. 265 to 237 is an 11% reduction in what you press and pull.

Three gymnastics goals are strength problems wearing skill costumes. A strict HSPU needs a press near 0.75-0.80x bodyweight; muscle-ups need heavy vertical pulling. Weighted pull-ups run twice weekly as a PRIMARY lift, and the strict press is primary on Tuesday. Bench dropped to one exposure to pay for it.
Weighted pull-ups are prescribed as total system load, so belt weight climbs as bodyweight falls. The cut pays the relative-strength goals twice.
Skill work is 8 min and 2 items: blocked weeks 1-3, variable by day from week 4. Blocked suits acquisition, variable retains and transfers.
Front squat and jerk need 28 weeks, not 15, so they start here.

blocks.name: Power & Olympic
blocks.goal: Snatch 225, C&J 295, peak vertical for the dunk, ring muscle-up.
principles: Power is the quality most punished by an energy deficit, so this block runs at maintenance.
Force-velocity curve covered deliberately: heavy front squats at the force end, Olympic lifts in the middle, sprints and jumps at the velocity end.
Weightlifting is a skill sport. Short sets at any intensity, per classical Prilepin-style guidance.
Plyometrics progress extensive (<=120 contacts/wk) to intensive (<=80 contacts/wk), always fresh.

blocks.name: Max Strength
principles: Only block running a surplus. The 10 lb gain is programmed, not a slip.
Zatsiorsky's three methods all used: maximal effort (Mon/Tue), repeated effort (Thu), dynamic effort (Fri).
Weekly 90%+ deadlift single from week 1, because expressing a maximum is a trainable skill and his tested single underperforms his rep max.
Bench gets three exposures because it recovers fast and rewards frequency for a skill-dependent lift.
Aerobic floor rises to 3 sessions here, not falls. Protecting the Crest.
Bench keeps its own lighter week at 8 so the two competing priorities never fully back off together. Weeks 4 and 7 are the declared block deloads, and both cut sets while holding percentage.

blocks.name: Speed & Bike
principles: A short speed block right after a max strength block converts force into velocity.
The two goals do not compete for a session. Track Mon/Thu, bike fills easy days and Saturday.
Five weeks of riding suffices only because eight months of easy aerobic volume went on the bike.
Maintenance strength holds intensity at 78-82% while set count drops.

blocks.name: Mountain
principles: The Crest is a durability problem, not a fitness problem.
Every Thursday runs the full descent. Eccentric exposure via the repeated bout effect is what protects the quads on the day.
Strength stays at 2 sessions of 2 lifts at 80%. Heavy strength work improves endurance performance.
Taper cuts volume 40-60% while holding intensity and frequency.
Fuelling rehearsed every long session. Gut absorption is trainable.
